varek.name: CONCURRENT · Grand Marshal Varek
varek.description: An elderly British field marshal of the Napoleonic wars. A deep, gravelly baritone, cold and stoic. He speaks slowly, with weight and long pauses, and every sentence falls to a low, final close, like a verdict. Clipped and unhurried; never warm, never raised.

ysolde.name: CONCURRENT · Viceroy Ysolde
ysolde.description: A middle-aged imperial viceroy, a woman with a low, cold, velvety voice and a faint Eastern European accent. Menacing and controlled, she lingers on possessive words like 'my' and 'mine'. Quiet contempt, never bright or friendly.

quill.name: CONCURRENT · Governor Quill
quill.description: A smug, middle-aged British colonial company governor: a merchant clerk turned conqueror. A precise, slightly nasal voice, pleased with himself, relishing every word about money. Each phrase descends at its end; no rising questions.

oren.name: CONCURRENT · Captain Oren
oren.description: A cocky British cavalry captain of noble birth, a young man in his twenties: eager, boastful and smarmy, a bit of a show-off. An upper-class accent and a quick, excited delivery that runs away with him. Swagger, not heroism.

hask.name: CONCURRENT · Commodore Hask
hask.description: A loud, salty old sea commodore called the Old Bear. A booming, gravelly, rough-edged West Country voice, belly laughs, shouted orders, full of gusto and sudden anger. Never polite, never quiet.

imre.name: CONCURRENT · Admiral Imre
imre.description: A calm elderly female admiral. A low, precise British voice, clipped and utterly confident, with a small calculating pause before each verdict. Cool and exact; never hesitant.
